complexity.notes: Clean and idiomatic. Worst case is O(n^2) because the hashed ints are input-controlled (adversarial multiples of 2**61-1 collide), though average lookups stay O(1). The follow-up's O(1)-space target is reachable in O(n) time via ||Floyd's cycle detection, reading the array as a linked list where nums[i] is the next pointer|| — but that trick is only valid while values stay in [1, n]; it does not survive generalization.
complexity.summary: Single pass that adds each value to a seen-set and returns the first value already present. Under the scaling note the duplicate's second occurrence sits about two thirds of the way through on average, so the scan does a fixed fraction of the array.
